data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'gygas', meaning 'earthborn' or 'jovial'. In ancient Greece, Gyges was a legendary king of Lydia, known for his cunning and earthy nature. The name Gyatt carries the meaning “Jovial, earthy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gyatt usually hope their child will grow to embody jovial, earthy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
